description.en: About 95% of Mars' air is carbon dioxide, which astronauts can't breathe. Oxygen has to be made or recycled.

fact.sourceName: Hoffman et al., Science Advances (2022), MOXIE first-year results

description.en: During a big dust storm in 2022, NASA switched off InSight's seismometer to save power, then turned it back on when the sky cleared.

fact.sourceName: NASA InSight mission (reported by Astronomy.com, Dec 2022)

description.en: In August 2015, astronauts on the ISS became the first to eat vegetables grown in space: red romaine lettuce.

fact.sourceName: NASA, Veggie plant growth system

description.en: NASA's Phoenix lander found a salt called perchlorate in Mars soil. It can be harmful in large amounts, so soil needs checking before growing food.

fact.sourceName: NASA/JPL, Phoenix mission results (Science papers, 2009); PBS NewsHour (Nov 2008)

description.en: On the Martian equator at noon, it would feel like spring at your feet but winter at your head, because the thin air holds little heat.

fact.sourceName: NASA Science, Mars Facts

description.en: NASA's InSight lander ran on solar panels. It was built for 2 years but worked for over 4, until dust piled up on its panels.

fact.sourceName: NASA InSight mission end announcement, 21 Dec 2022

description.en: Curiosity measured radiation on Mars: about 0.67 millisieverts a day on the surface, similar to what astronauts get on the ISS.

fact.sourceName: Hassler et al., Science (2013), doi:10.1126/science.1244797

description.en: Space chile peppers grew about 2 weeks slower than on Earth. The crew ate the first harvest on 29 October 2021.

fact.sourceName: NASA, "NASA's Second Pepper Harvest Sets Record on Space Station"

description.en: NASA tested a small nuclear reactor called Kilopower. It can make up to 10 kilowatts for at least 10 years, and four could power an outpost.

fact.sourceName: NASA release, "Demonstration Proves Nuclear Fission System Can Provide Space Exploration Power" (3 May 2018)

description.en: NASA's Phoenix lander landed near the Martian north pole in 2008 and confirmed there is water ice just under the soil.

fact.sourceName: NASA/JPL, Phoenix mission update (Sep 2008)

description.en: The ISS recycles about 98% of its water, including sweat and urine. Each astronaut uses about a gallon a day.

fact.sourceName: NASA ECLSS water recovery release, 20 Jun 2023

description.en: When dust covered InSight's solar panels, NASA trickled dirt from its scoop on windy days so falling grains would sweep dust away.

fact.sourceName: NASA InSight mission end announcement, 21 Dec 2022

description.en: Curiosity's radiation detector once saw a spike on Mars caused by a burst of particles from the Sun.

fact.sourceName: Hassler et al., Science (2013), doi:10.1126/science.1244797

description.en: On the ISS, a scrubber removes the carbon dioxide astronauts breathe out. A reactor then turns it and hydrogen into water.

fact.sourceName: NASA Marshall, Environmental Control and Life Support System fact sheet

description.en: Plants in NASA's Advanced Plant Habitat on the ISS grow under red, blue, green and white LED lights.

fact.sourceName: NASA, "Astronauts Harvest Radish Crop on International Space Station" (Dec 2020)

description.en: NASA's DONKI database tracks solar flares and solar storms, and estimates when a storm cloud may reach planets like Mars.

fact.sourceName: NASA CCMC, DONKI (Moon-to-Mars Space Weather Analysis Office)

description.en: A tiny machine on Perseverance called MOXIE made 122 grams of oxygen from Mars' air, about what a small dog breathes in 10 hours.

fact.sourceName: NASA MOXIE completion release, 6 Sep 2023

description.en: In May 2024 a huge solar storm hit Mars. An astronaut next to Curiosity would have received radiation equal to 30 chest X-rays.

fact.sourceName: NASA/JPL, "NASA Watches Mars Light Up During Epic Solar Storm" (10 Jun 2024)

description.en: NASA grew radishes on the ISS because they're ready in just 27 days. More than 180 sensors watched them grow.

fact.sourceName: NASA, "Astronauts Harvest Radish Crop on International Space Station" (Dec 2020)

description.en: Opportunity was built for 90 days but worked over 14 years, until a planet-wide dust storm in 2018 blocked the Sun.

fact.sourceName: NASA, Opportunity mission end announcement (13 Feb 2019)
